content_units: 7-Day Lower-Sodium Meal Week at a Glance

For a 67-year-old with mild high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes on metformin, a practical week of meals should emphasize   low sodium, steady carbohydrates, high fiber, lean protein, and simple prep  . This outline avoids grapefruit, uses familiar home cooking, and keeps meals moderate rather than restrictive.
Context for this plan
- General education only; not a substitute for personalized medical advice.
- A reasonable target is often   about 1,500-2,000 mg sodium/day  , depending on clinician guidance.
- Meals below aim for   minimal added salt  , with flavor from herbs, lemon, garlic, onion, vinegar, and spices.
7-Day Meal Outline
Option 1:   Day 1   Oatmeal & baked salmon day     Fiber-forward start
- Breakfast: Oatmeal cooked with milk or unsweetened soy milk, topped with berries, chia seeds, and a few walnuts.
- Lunch: Turkey and avocado whole-grain sandwich with lettuce, tomato, and no-salt mustard; side of cucumber slices.
- Dinner: Baked salmon, quinoa, and roasted broccoli with olive oil, garlic, and black pepper.
- Snack ideas: Plain Greek yogurt; small apple with peanut butter.
Option 2:   Day 2   Eggs, soup, and chicken     Simple batch-cook friendly
- Breakfast: Vegetable omelet with spinach, mushrooms, and onions; one slice whole-grain toast.
- Lunch: Homemade lentil soup made without salty broth; side salad with olive oil and vinegar.
- Dinner: Skinless roasted chicken thigh or breast, baked sweet potato, and green beans.
- Snack ideas: Carrot sticks with hummus; pear.
Option 3:   Day 3   Yogurt bowl & stir-fry day     Balanced carbs and protein
- Breakfast: Plain Greek yogurt with sliced strawberries, ground flaxseed, and a spoon of oats.
- Lunch: Tuna salad made with no-salt-added tuna, plain yogurt or light mayo, celery, and lemon; served in a whole-wheat wrap or lettuce cups.
- Dinner: Chicken and vegetable stir-fry with bell peppers, snap peas, and brown rice; use low-sodium soy sauce sparingly or coconut aminos.
- Snack ideas: Unsalted nuts; celery with peanut butter.
Option 4:   Day 4   Cottage cheese & bean chili day     High satiety, easy leftovers
- Breakfast: Low-sodium cottage cheese or plain yogurt with peach slices and cinnamon.
- Lunch: Quinoa bowl with black beans, tomato, cucumber, red onion, and olive oil-lime dressing.
- Dinner: Homemade turkey chili with no-salt-added beans and tomatoes; side of steamed spinach or mixed vegetables.
- Snack ideas: Small orange; a few whole-grain crackers with unsalted nut butter.
Option 5:   Day 5   Peanut butter toast & cod     Very simple prep
- Breakfast: Whole-grain toast with natural peanut butter and banana slices.
- Lunch: Leftover turkey chili or lentil soup; side salad.
- Dinner: Baked cod or other white fish, barley or brown rice, and sautéed zucchini with garlic.
- Snack ideas: Plain yogurt; berries.
Option 6:   Day 6   Smoothie & meatball day     Comfort food with lighter swaps
- Breakfast: Smoothie with spinach, berries, plain yogurt, chia seeds, and unsweetened milk.
- Lunch: Egg salad made with yogurt and mustard on whole-grain bread; tomato slices on the side.
- Dinner: Homemade turkey meatballs over whole-wheat pasta or spaghetti squash with no-salt-added tomato sauce and a side salad.
- Snack ideas: Unsalted almonds; sliced bell peppers.
Option 7:   Day 7   Oats & sheet-pan dinner     Easy finish to the week
- Breakfast: Overnight oats with cinnamon, diced apple, and chopped walnuts.
- Lunch: Chickpea salad with cucumber, parsley, tomato, olive oil, lemon, and a small whole-grain pita.
- Dinner: Sheet-pan chicken or tofu with cauliflower, carrots, and Brussels sprouts; small serving of brown rice.
- Snack ideas: Kiwi or apple; plain popcorn without much salt.
Grocery Themes for Simple Home Cooking
Core foods to keep on hand
-   Proteins:   chicken breast or thighs, salmon, cod, eggs, turkey, tofu, no-salt-added tuna, plain Greek yogurt
-   High-fiber carbs:   oats, quinoa, brown rice, barley, whole-grain bread, whole-wheat pasta, sweet potatoes
-   Beans and legumes:   lentils, black beans, chickpeas, low-sodium or no-salt-added canned options
-   Vegetables:   spinach, broccoli, green beans, zucchini, carrots, bell peppers, onions, mushrooms, tomatoes, cucumbers
-   Fruits:   berries, apples, pears, peaches, oranges, kiwi, bananas
-   Healthy fats:   olive oil, avocado, walnuts, almonds, chia, flaxseed, natural peanut butter
-   Flavor builders:   garlic, lemon, lime, vinegar, pepper, paprika, cumin, oregano, basil, parsley, cinnamon
Helpful low-sodium pantry swaps
- Choose   no-salt-added canned beans and tomatoes
- Use   low-sodium broth   or homemade broth
- Pick   plain frozen vegetables   instead of seasoned ones
- Limit packaged sauces, deli meats, canned soups, and frozen dinners
- Use   low-sodium soy sauce   very lightly, if at all
Key Nutrition Points to Watch
Blood pressure priorities
-   Sodium:   Main goal is lowering sodium from processed foods, canned soups, deli meats, salty snacks, sauces, and restaurant meals.
-   Potassium-rich foods:   Beans, leafy greens, sweet potatoes, yogurt, and many fruits may help support blood pressure balance.
-   Weight-friendly portions:   Even modest weight loss can help blood pressure.
Diabetes-friendly priorities
-   Carbohydrate consistency:   Spread carbs across the day instead of having one very large carb-heavy meal.
-   Pair carbs with protein or fat:   Oatmeal with nuts, fruit with yogurt, toast with peanut butter.
-   Fiber:   Aim for oats, beans, vegetables, berries, and whole grains to help with glucose control and fullness.
-   Watch hidden sugars:   Flavored yogurt, sweet cereals, bottled dressings, sauces, and smoothies can add more sugar than expected.
Meal-building guide
- Fill about   half the plate with non-starchy vegetables
- Use   one palm-size serving of protein
- Keep starches to a   moderate portion  , such as 1 small sweet potato or about 1/2 to 1 cup cooked grain
- Favor   water, milk, or unsweetened drinks   over sweet beverages
